description: A Reactome pathway group: a macromolecular complex or a set of alternative complexes. Cellular-compartment and modification variants are separate nodes, distinguished by their Reactome stable IDs.

common_properties.name: identifier
common_properties.description: Reactome stable ID prefixed with reactome:, for example reactome:R-HSA-389357.

common_properties.name: reactome_id
common_properties.description: Bare Reactome stable ID, for example R-HSA-389357.

common_properties.name: name
common_properties.description: Reactome display name; the bare stable ID is used when a display name is missing.

common_properties.name: version
common_properties.description: Reactome release number in which the node was last seen.

common_properties.name: sources
common_properties.description: Data sources contributing the node; Reactome for this type.

common_properties.name: last_updated
common_properties.description: Time the node was created or last updated.

source_contributions.scope: Complexes associated with the human BioPAX export’s Signaling Pathways (R-HSA-162582), Immune System (R-HSA-168256), and Diseases of signal transduction by growth factor receptors and second messengers (R-HSA-5663202) hierarchies, including descendant pathways. Scope includes complexes used by events, their catalysts and regulators, and active units, as well as nested complexes and complexes reached through entity sets. Non-human stable IDs, including viral complexes used in human pathways, are retained.
source_contributions.description: Complexes with components represent entities present together; component membership expresses physical part-of relationships. Complex-typed sets represent alternatives and have no member edges: their member complexes are separate nodes without links to the set. Non-complex entity sets are excluded and their members do not substitute for them in participation or membership relationships. Component links cover proteins, compounds, DNA-associated genes, and other pathway groups when represented in SPOKE; RNA and generic entities have no component links. Catalysis and regulation relationships are absent even when their complexes are represented. Compartment, stoichiometry, and a complex-versus-set flag are not stored as properties.

properties.name: synonyms
properties.description: Reactome alternate names, excluding values equal to the display name without regard to case.
